clue.text: Excerpt from FIFA in the art editorial showing cowardice

indicators.note: an excerpt is a passage lifted out of a longer text, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: read straight through the run of letters across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A newspaper art editorial carries a timid piece about football's governing body.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of FIFA through 'in the art' into the start of 'editorial'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking courage, easily frightened, is described as cowardly or timid in this compound adjective.

clue.text: Daughter replaces wife in distant unit

indicators.note: replaces means one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: far away means distant

explanation.surface: A daughter taking over from a wife who has moved far away.
explanation.definitionFit: The farad is the SI measure of electrical capacitance, named after Michael Faraday; the faraday is also a unit of electric charge.

clue.text: Current row about Switzerland is increasingly irritating

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is wrapped round another

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
CH is Switzerland's international code (Confoederatio Helvetica)

explanation.surface: An ongoing quarrel involving the Swiss keeps getting more annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' wants to be an argument, but here it is a line of seats. 'Current' is not about electricity's flow in general but its symbol in physics formulae.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchy can mean irritating or prickly, and the comparative form describes something becoming more so.

clue.text: Toy towers rebuilt as many houses

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase describing houses, as the answer is

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A child's toy castle is rebuilt to look like a row of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As many houses' means 'as many houses are': the answer is a typical description of an ordinary home.
explanation.definitionFit: Most ordinary homes have a ground floor and one upper floor, so that is how many houses are built.

clue.text: Communication area within cycling distance

indicators.note: within means placed inside, so the area letter goes inside the other piece
cycling means moving round, so a letter goes from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: a mile is a distance

explanation.surface: Messages sent to everyone living within cycling distance of the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the final E of MILE to the front to give EMIL, and 'within' puts A inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message, one form of communication.

clue.text: Government in Middle East overrun by nation in uprising

indicators.note: something overrun is swamped and surrounded, so one piece ends up inside another
in a down clue an uprising lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Niger is a West African country
ME is the abbreviation for the Middle East

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern government is overthrown by a country in revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Government' looks like the regime being toppled, but it is the definition; the nation is the African country, not one in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Regimen is an old word for rule or system of government, as well as a prescribed course such as a diet.

clue.text: Where to buy drinks pass after Maine brought back Prohibition

indicators.note: after means following, so the piece before it in the clue goes second in the answer
something brought back travels the other way, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
a bar serves drinks
to pass a turn or move on is to go

explanation.surface: Maine reintroduced Prohibition, cutting off the supply of drinks — a nod to the state's early dry laws.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P makes Prohibition look like America's 1920s alcohol ban, but it is just a general ban here.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade with a particular country, so it is a prohibition.

clue.text: A rebel Lord with a local area prize for playing the part?

parts.note: taken as written
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450
'Lord!' and 'My!' are both exclamations of surprise
taken as written
a ward is a local electoral district

explanation.surface: A rebellious peer wins a local prize for his acting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord' looks like a nobleman, but it is an exclamation. Jack Cade was the leader of a 15th-century English peasants' revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is awarded for screen acting, among other things, so this is a prize for playing a role well.

clue.text: City no longer probing source of chocolate liqueur

indicators.note: a probe pushes into something, so one piece is inserted into another

parts.note: cacao beans are what chocolate is made from
Ur was an ancient Mesopotamian city that no longer exists

explanation.surface: A city has stopped investigating where its chocolate liqueur comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks a city of the ancient world, the Sumerian one crossword setters love because it is so short.
explanation.definitionFit: Curaçao is an orange-flavoured spirit-based drink named after the Caribbean island where the bitter oranges grow.

clue.text: Symbolic system upset, say, City supporter

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: e.g. means 'for example', as 'say' does
LA is Los Angeles
a bra is an item of support underwear

explanation.surface: A football fan of a City side is upset, perhaps by the club's system of play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City supporter' reads like a football fan, but it splits into LA and a piece of underwear. Both 'say' and 'City' are turned round together.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is the branch of mathematics that uses letters and symbols to stand for numbers in formulae and equations.

clue.text: Playing hog in NY stage musical

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hogs the limelight in a New York stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' seems to describe the musical but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter's 1934 Broadway show about a transatlantic liner is a famous example of the genre.

clue.text: Addis Ababa teacher at first mishandled someone abandoning tradition

indicators.note: something mishandled is treated roughly and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening, so only the initial letters are kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the second word of the capital's name
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A teacher in Ethiopia's capital mishandled a pupil who rejects convention.
explanation.walkthrough: The city's name splits: its first word is used whole, while the second, like 'teacher', gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was an early twentieth-century art movement that deliberately rejected conventional artistic values and logic.

clue.text: Hit Star Wars character is a fish

parts.note: to lamp someone is slang for punching them
Rey is the heroine of the later Star Wars films

explanation.surface: A hit Star Wars character turns out to be a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' looks like an adjective for a successful film, but it is a verb meaning to punch.
explanation.definitionFit: This jawless, eel-like water creature sucks onto other animals with a round toothed mouth.

clue.text: One wearing chain mail, half-cut Rovers player in a spin

indicators.note: half-cut means half the word is cut away, leaving its first two letters

parts.note: the clue word itself, before it is cut

indicators.note: in a spin means turned round, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Roy of the Rovers is a long-running British comic strip about a footballer, Roy Race

explanation.surface: Someone in chain mail, drunk, playing for Rovers and spinning about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chain mail' is a false phrase: 'chain' ends the definition, as a mayor wears a chain of office. 'half-cut' looks like drunk but trims MAIL to MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A British mayor traditionally wears a ceremonial chain of office, so is one wearing a chain.

clue.text: Self-inflicted error, having published entertaining joke that's spicy

definitions.note: stands for 'something that's spicy', a noun like the answer

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a paper that ran a story published it
OG is an own goal in football
to josh is to tease or joke

explanation.surface: A writer makes a gaffe by printing a racy, spicy joke.
explanation.walkthrough: In football an own goal is the classic self-inflicted error, abbreviated in match reports. The definition is the noun phrase 'that's spicy', meaning a spicy dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This Kashmiri lamb curry, cooked in a rich red sauce, is a staple of British Indian restaurants and is notably hot.

clue.text: Bagel uses spread, not impossible to get

indicators.note: things spread are scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bagel calls for some spread, which is not hard to come by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a noun for butter or cream cheese, but it is the verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: If an answer can be worked out by intelligent guesswork, it is something a solver could plausibly get.

clue.text: Jaguar backing what goes over wheel, for example

indicators.note: to back something is to stand behind it, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: a wheel arch is the curved part of a car body over each wheel
the E-Type is a famous Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: A car part sitting above a wheel, as on a Jaguar.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jaguar is the car, not the cat; it comes after the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is a perfect model or typical specimen of something, so it serves as a standard example.

clue.text: Fine cup of tea with unwanted visitors

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea
lice are uninvited guests in the hair

explanation.surface: A dainty cup of tea served to guests nobody invited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwanted visitors' sounds like gatecrashers at a tea party, but they are parasites.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a large ornate goblet, especially the one used for wine at Communion, so it is an elegant drinking vessel.

clue.text: Interminable, as week is compared to Saturday and Sunday

definitions.text: as week is compared to Saturday and Sunday
definitions.meaning: second, playful meaning: the word for the days is the weekend word with its last part taken off

explanation.walkthrough: Saturday and Sunday make the weekend; the rest of the week is the word 'weekend' lacking its last three letters, read literally as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never stops or has no limit can be called interminable or unending.

clue.text: What's more or less encapsulated by "soft nut"?

definitions.text: What's more or less encapsulated by "soft nut"?

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction to play softly

indicators.note: a capsule encloses its contents, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: in printing an en space is called a nut
ca (circa) means approximately

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what is roughly contained in a soft nut.
explanation.walkthrough: Printers call an en space a nut, to tell it from an em, the mutton. Read whole, the clue asks for something that is, more or less, a soft nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit of a hickory tree from North America has a thin shell and an oily kernel, and is a fairly soft eating nut.

clue.text: Word perhaps for chickpea, rather rarely

parts.note: pro means in favour of
gram is an old name for the chickpea, now seldom used except for its flour

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the word for chickpea, which comes up rather rarely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Word' is Microsoft Word, the software, not a vocabulary item; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Microsoft's word-processing package is one example of software, a set of instructions run on a computer.

clue.text: Agree, chapter one's supported by article in Bild

indicators.note: in a down clue what is supported sits on top, so one piece goes above the other

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for chapter
'one's' as 'one is' becomes 'I am', shortened
ein is the German for 'a'; Bild is a German newspaper

explanation.surface: A German tabloid article backs up the first chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' expands to 'one is', which a person saying it of themselves turns into I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To chime in with someone is to concur with or echo their opinion, so it can mean to agree.

clue.text: Boy whose fortunes changed after originally dropping racket

parts.note: à la means in the manner of, or after

indicators.note: what is there originally comes at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A boy's luck turned once he stopped playing with his tennis racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a time word but is à la, 'in the style of'. 'Racket' is noise, not sports equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: In the pantomime and folk tale, a poor youth becomes rich and marries a princess thanks to a magic lamp and genie.

clue.text: Benjamin ordered to cede MBE after training spy

indicators.note: ordered here means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged
to cede is to give up, so these letters are removed from the pool
training shapes something into a new form, supporting the rearrangement

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
the letters to be given up, taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Benjamin is told to hand back his honour after training as a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: MBE is a British honour (Member of the Order of the British Empire). Take M, B and E out of BENJAMIN and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninja were covert agents in feudal Japan, used for espionage and assassination, so a ninja is a kind of spy.

clue.text: What happens when In the Bleak Midwinter immediately interrupts carol

definitions.text: What happens when In the Bleak Midwinter

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a synonym for at once

explanation.surface: A favourite carol cuts in suddenly on another one.
explanation.walkthrough: The carol 'In the Bleak Midwinter' has the line 'snow had fallen, snow on snow'. 'Carol' is the verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol depicts a frozen winter landscape where flakes are falling, so the weather it describes is wintry precipitation.

clue.text: One way to reverse mood — McDonalds?

indicators.note: reversing is going backwards, so the letters are read from end to start

parts.note: Roman numeral one
Rd is the abbreviation for road
a vein is a mood or humour, as in 'in a playful vein'

explanation.surface: A way to turn a bad mood round: a trip to McDonald's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' looks like a driving term but applies to the first two pieces only. The question mark shows McDonald's is just one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Some fast-food chains let customers order and eat without leaving their cars, at a restaurant built for that purpose.

clue.text: Problem turned round by your correspondent, south-east Asian

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: 'there's the rub' — a rub is a difficulty
the setter refers to themselves
SE is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A letter-writer from south-east Asia has a problem turned around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South-east Asian' reads as one phrase, but the compass point belongs to the wordplay and the definition is just 'Asian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma, now officially Myanmar, is a country of the Asian mainland, and its people and language are called by this adjective.

clue.text: Writer possibly warm, as pen repeatedly brandished

indicators.note: brandished, waved about, means the letters are shaken into a new order
repeatedly means the word pen appears twice

explanation.surface: A writer, warm to the task, waves pen after pen about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' doubles PEN; 'brandished' scrambles WARM, AS and PENPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist on a daily paper is one kind of writer, hence 'possibly'.
